raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

The CuTe DSL's `Arch` enum starts at `sm_80`. On a Turing part (cc 7.5: T4, RTX 20xx), compiling any DSL kernel dies inside the DSL:

```
.../cutlass/base_dsl/enums.py:110: KeyError: 'sm_75'
```

`cudnn.frost.buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(device_cc)` is the target half of `cudnn.frost.cutedsl_runtime_available`, and the gate callers consult before compiling. It only checked cc 10.7, so on cc 7.5 it reported no problem.

As a result, callers that already have a torch fallback for "the DSL cannot target this GPU" took the DSL path anyway and crashed instead of falling back:
- `cudnn.sdpa.packed_lse`
- `cudnn.sdpa.varlen_metadata`

## Change

`cutedsl_arch_requirement_error` now refuses a part below cc 8.0 by name, without importing the DSL. This has two effects:
- `cutedsl_runtime_available(cc)` now reads False on cc < 8.0. This is the correct answer, but it is a behavior change for consumers of the probe, such as FlashInfer.
- The two fallbacks above now take their torch path.

Nothing changes on cc 8.0 and newer. The cc 10.7 check is unchanged.

Other edits:
- `test_flashinfer_consumed_surface.py`: the arch-aware probe test now covers cc 7.5. A new host-only test checks cc 7.5 / 7.0 / 6.1: the message names the part, the DSL is never asked, the probe reads False, and cc 8.0 still passes.
- The rule is also stated in `python/cudnn/AGENTS.md` and `docs/utilities/python_graph_and_execution_backends.md`.

## Testing

RTX 2060 (sm_75), cuDNN 9.27, CuTe DSL 4.8.1, develop e77fe6d4:

| | failed | passed | skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_packed_lse`, `test_varlen_metadata`, `test_flashinfer_consumed_surface`, base | 26 | 41 | 16 |
| same files, this PR | 0 | 41 | 45 |

No change on cc 8.0 and newer. A100 (sm_80) runs the same three files plus `triangle_attention/cutedsl/test_api.py` and `test/python/QSA`: base 115 passed / 281 skipped, this PR 118 passed / 281 skipped. The 3 extra passes are the new cc 7.5 / 7.0 / 6.1 cases.

`black 26.3.1 --line-length 160 --fast` is clean.

## Out of scope

Some direct-compile suites call `cute.compile` without consulting this gate:
- the `gated_attention_block` kernel tests;
- the FROST GEMM per-K tests.

They still fail on cc 7.5 with the same `KeyError`.

The triangle-attention prefix-length tests do consult the gate. They now fail with a typed `NotImplementedError` naming the missing target instead of a `KeyError`, with the same failure count.

Adding skips to those suites is separate work.

 | does the native SDPA binder honor a packed-split / stride contract? | `cudnn._pybind_module._SdpaThdBinder.supports_stats_stride_override`, `.supports_nonpaged_packed_split`, `.supports_paged_split_sink`, ... (static read-only properties, `True`) | `"<cap>" in cudnn.sdpa_capabilities()` -- the frozenset of every `supports_<cap>` flag the build provides; append-only, never renamed |

 | can the cuDNN backend still serve this graph? | `graph.backend_plan_entries()` after `create_execution_plans` (`[]` = declined, guarded or not installed) | the same method, documented above |
-| can the FROST engines run on this install, for this GPU? | `cudnn.frost.buffers.cutedsl_state()` / `cutedsl_too_old(version)` / `CUTEDSL_MIN_VERSION` -- the version half only | `cudnn.frost.cutedsl_runtime_available(device_cc=None)`: the version half, plus -- given a `(major, minor)` cc -- the target half (`cutedsl_arch_requirement_error`). **The floor is 4.7.0 everywhere and 4.8.0 on cc 10.7** (the first public wheel whose `Arch` knows `sm_107a`): a device-blind probe on a cc 10.7 part with a 4.7.x DSL says True while every FROST row declines, so pass the GPU you route to |

 | the unified attention implementation, the graph helpers, the caller hints | `cudnn.attention_implementation.UNIFIED`, `cudnn.graph_cache(key_fn=)`, `cudnn.jit(heur_modes=)`, `cudnn.graph(handle, **graph_kwargs)`, `cudnn.pygraph(is_override_shape_enabled=, is_cuda_graph_replay_expected=)` | already public; listed so the pin covers them |

@@ -734,8 +734,9 @@ treatment at the caller boundary.**
   -> False cell of the arch-aware probe. Renaming one means updating
   FlashInfer's fallbacks first; that test failing is the reminder. The runtime
   probe takes the part because the DSL floor is 4.7.0 everywhere and 4.8.0 on
-  cc 10.7 (Rule 7): a device-blind "available" is the blind spot that routes a
-  cc 10.7 graph to the backend engine.
+  cc 10.7, and no DSL has a target below cc 8.0 (Rule 7): a device-blind
+  "available" is the blind spot that routes a cc 10.7 graph to the backend
+  engine.
 
 **Rule 10 — a kwarg that makes a graph ineligible for the python engines is
 read by the family's analyzer under the spelling of EVERY op that takes it.**

@@ -39,6 +39,7 @@ def cutedsl_runtime_available(device_cc=None) -> bool:
       part: cc 10.7 needs a DSL whose ``Arch`` has ``sm_107a`` (the public 4.8.0
       wheel is the first), so **the floor is 4.7.0 everywhere and 4.8.0 on
       cc 10.7** (:func:`cudnn.frost.buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error`).
+      A part below cc 8.0 has no target in any DSL and reads False.
       This half imports the DSL once, on a cc 10.7 part only.
 
     A device-blind call (``device_cc=None``) answers the version half alone:

@@ -615,8 +615,12 @@ def cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(device_cc):
 
     The TARGET half of the public probe :func:`cudnn.frost.cutedsl_runtime_available`: cc 10.7 needs a DSL whose
     ``Arch`` knows ``sm_107a`` (the public 4.8.0 wheel is the first), so the floor is 4.7.0 everywhere and 4.8.0 on
-    cc 10.7. None when the part is not cc 10.7 or the target is present; otherwise the message names the installed
-    DSL."""
+    cc 10.7. A part below cc 8.0 has no target in any CuTe DSL (its ``Arch`` starts at ``sm_80``; compiling for a
+    Turing part raises ``KeyError: 'sm_75'`` inside the DSL), so it is refused without importing the DSL. None when
+    the target is present; otherwise the message names the part or the installed DSL."""
+    if device_cc is not None and tuple(device_cc) < (8, 0):
+        major, minor = device_cc
+        return f"the CuTe DSL has no target below SM80 (its Arch starts at sm_80); found cc {major}.{minor}"
     if device_cc != (10, 7) or _cutedsl_has_sm107():
         return None
     _, version = cutedsl_state()

@@ -198,7 +198,8 @@ def test_cutedsl_runtime_available_is_arch_aware(dsl_state, label, installed, ve
     probe = cudnn.frost.cutedsl_runtime_available
     assert probe() is blind, label
     assert probe(None) is blind, label
-    assert probe((8, 0)) is cc100, label  # no target gate below cc 10.7
+    assert probe((7, 5)) is False, label  # no DSL has a target below sm_80
+    assert probe((8, 0)) is cc100, label  # no target gate from cc 8.0 up to cc 10.7
     assert probe((10, 0)) is cc100, label
     assert probe((10, 7)) is cc107, label
     assert probe([10, 7]) is cc107, label  # a list spells the same part
@@ -213,6 +214,18 @@ def test_the_blind_spot_cell_cc107_with_a_47x_dsl(dsl_state):
     assert buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error((10, 0)) is None
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cc", [(7, 5), (7, 0), (6, 1)])
+def test_a_part_below_sm80_has_no_dsl_target(dsl_state, monkeypatch, cc):
+    """The DSL's Arch starts at sm_80: compiling for a Turing part raised ``KeyError: 'sm_75'`` inside the DSL. The gate
+    refuses it by name without asking the DSL, so callers with a fallback (packed LSE, varlen metadata) take it."""
+    dsl_state(True, (PUBLIC_DSL, "4.8.1"), True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(buffers, "_cutedsl_has_sm107", lambda: pytest.fail("the DSL was asked about a part below sm_80"))
+    assert buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(cc) == f"the CuTe DSL has no target below SM80 (its Arch starts at sm_80); found cc {cc[0]}.{cc[1]}"
+    assert buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(list(cc)) is not None
+    assert cudnn.frost.cutedsl_runtime_available(cc) is False
+    assert buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error((8, 0)) is None
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [(10, 7, 0), (10,), 107, "10.7", (10.5, 7)])
 def test_cutedsl_runtime_available_refuses_a_malformed_cc(dsl_state, bad):
     """A cc that is not a pair of integers is refused, never silently read as 'not cc 10.7'."""
